### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `627f3686d4f7be60ed324b49e695723555dea980` — the merge of head `8a1365b28e5ad21d739795f245ccc98e29c5e520` into base `077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 627f3686d4f7be60ed324b49e695723555dea980 && git checkout 627f3686d4f7be60ed324b49e695723555dea980
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881 8a1365b28e5ad21d739795f245ccc98e29c5e520 && git checkout -B drift-repro 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881 && git merge --no-ff 8a1365b28e5ad21d739795f245ccc98e29c5e520

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `816c01e8a144ce03c1337303142a490b320a3582`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/knowledge-settings-retired-keys.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-visibility-declaration.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/__tests__/settings-door.testkit.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/{ar,de,en,es-ES,fr,ja-JP,ko,pt-BR,ru,zh-CN,zh-Hant}.ts + (cited, read on `origin/main`, not reviewed) packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-settings-contribution.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts, packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-read-door.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/cloud-managed-settings.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsView.tsx

Inputs read: card #37104 body and its four comments (triage 7143863466, unblock 7199765341, claim 7199811101, dev report 7201999210; no ruling and no earlier record on the thread), PR #37668 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...816c01e8a`, and the 55 check-runs on the head (40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure; Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 10/10, Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness all success).

### ① Derived judgments

- `PUT /api/settings/knowledge` accept set shrinks by `adapter`, `over_fetch`, `enforce_rls`: each is now `400 UNKNOWN_KEY`. Right. It is the generic undeclared-key answer of `settings-routes.ts` (`UnknownKeyError` to `UNKNOWN_KEY`), no new code path, and the refusal is of the WHOLE body (see N2).
- `GET /api/settings/knowledge` serves three keys (`turso_url`, `turso_auth_token`, `chunk_target`), two groups, no banner, no `visible` predicate. Right; pinned by exact list in `knowledge.manifest.test.ts` and through the real route in the new pin file.
- `POST /api/settings/knowledge/test` answers from the two Turso fields only; the `memory` warning and the `Unknown adapter` error answers are gone, so a stored `adapter = ragflow` moves from an error answer to the Turso form check. Right, and declared on the `Clause-②:` line.
- Manifest `version` 3 to 4. Right: `settings-manifest.zod.ts:798` says "Increment when keys are renamed/removed".
- Public exports of `@objectstack/service-settings` (`knowledgeSettingsManifest`, `knowledgeTestActionHandler`) keep name and signature. No `packages/spec` schema, error-code ledger row or metadata type moves. Right.
- Visibility-predicate corpus 83 to 79 (Turso group, its two keys, `over_fetch`). Right, counted against the four removed `data.adapter` predicates on `main`.
- Locale bundles: all eleven drop the `adapter` and `permissions` groups, the `adapter` / `over_fetch` / `enforce_rls` keys and the whole `banners` block of the `knowledge` namespace, and all eleven gain the PostgreSQL sentence on the Turso group (each bundle's `knowledge` block read on the head). Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-settings: patch`, title with `!`, a **BREAKING** paragraph, in pre mode: the same level and form as the merged precedent for this very door (`.changeset/pre/37004-retire-knowledge-ragflow.md`), and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. It is the only package whose code changes. Matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is the correct declaration, present on the PR body and the changeset with the same narrowed list (PUT refusal with its status and code, GET no longer serving, the test door's changed answers). `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: a settings manifest is a runtime registration, nothing `objectstack migrate meta` reads names these keys, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` says so. The changeset names what a caller who PUTs the keys gets (refused as an undeclared key, `400 UNKNOWN_KEY` on the clause line), says stored rows stay, and gives the tidy-up (delete the three `knowledge` rows from `sys_platform_setting`). One gap in the migration note is N2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none filed. Nothing to escalate.
- Dev flag, `adapter` removed rather than shown read-only: accepted. The card allows either ("or is removed"), no specifier renders a runtime value, and the per-source store is already answered by `index_status` / `os knowledge status`.
- Dev flag, `spec-property-retirement` does not apply: agreed, these are manifest keys, not `packages/spec` properties.
- Dev flag, the unlocked second dogfood run started by a heredoc and stopped: a process deviation with no effect on the tree; nothing cited from it. The gate verdicts used here are the head's check-runs.
- Dev out-of-scope note (the cloud per-organization sentence, not filed): answered in seat question 5, card-worthy.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the platform's own refusal real; it takes no delivered capability away. Read on `origin/main`:

- `over_fetch`: zero occurrences outside the manifest, its test, the locale bundles and changelogs (`git grep` over the whole tree, snake and camel spellings). Search widens by the constants `SEARCH_FIRST_ROUND_FACTOR = 5` and `SEARCH_REFILL_FACTOR = 20` (`knowledge-service.ts:2478,2486`, used at :1362 and :1380).
- `enforce_rls`: zero occurrences outside the same files. `applyPermissionFilter` (`knowledge-service.ts:2188`) reads no setting: it passes only an explicit `isSystem` context, fails closed with no context or no engine, and otherwise re-reads every object-source hit as the caller.
- `adapter`: read by `knowledgeTestActionHandler` and by the four `data.adapter` visibility predicates of the same manifest, nothing else. The only `settings.get('knowledge', …)` callers are `knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts:356` (`turso_url`, `turso_auth_token` only) and `knowledge-service-plugin.ts:474` (`chunk_target`); nothing calls `getNamespace('knowledge')` outside a test.

So each removed key was a declared capability never delivered, retired at its declaration, which is the ADR-0049 remove arm and what the card orders for `enforce_rls`. Attempts to break it: a stored row is never resolved for an undeclared key (pin test, an encrypted row with a dangling handle included); the Console keeps drafts in component state and sends dirty keys only, so no cached form re-sends a retired key; nothing keys on the manifest version.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — On PostgreSQL the page now always shows `turso_url`, `turso_auth_token` and a Test connection button that nothing reads there (before, the group was hidden unless `adapter = turso` was chosen). The description says so honestly, and the card's acceptance (a named reader per key) is met, so this is not a defect of this PR; but the topic's goal is a page without unread keys. The embedder section already shows the pattern (`withAiEmbedderSection`, contributed with its service): the Turso group could be contributed by the store that reads it. Follow-up card. The sentence is also inexact at two edges: an in-memory platform database mounts the store with a fixed `:memory:` URL and no `urlFromSettings` (`capability-composition.ts:345`), so the fields are not read there either; and a host that registers `KnowledgeTursoPlugin` by hand with `urlFromSettings` on PostgreSQL does read them.
- N2 (nit) — The changeset and PR body say the write "is refused" but not that the refusal is of the whole body: a script that sends `adapter` together with `turso_url` and `turso_auth_token` in one PUT (the natural shape while the Turso fields were gated on `adapter = turso`) now saves neither, and the store opens its default file at the next boot. The 400 is loud, so no silent loss; the migration note should say "drop the three keys from the body". Prose-face fix or accepted deviation.
- N3 (nit) — "not served … reported nowhere" holds for the settings door. The stored `enforce_rls = false` row is still listed by the data API's diagnostic grid of `sys_platform_setting` to a holder of the namespace's read permission (`settings-read-door.ts`), where it can still be misread as a live switch. The changeset already gives the delete; the pin test title "reaches no reader" asserts only the GET door. Accepted deviation.
- N4 (nit) — Two unchanged tests still post the retired `adapter` to the test door (`knowledge-settings-default-absent.pin.test.ts:130`, service-knowledge's `knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts`). They pass because the handler ignores it; stale fixtures only. Follow-up or leave.

Seat questions:

1. Verified on `origin/main` as listed above: nothing read `over_fetch`, nothing read `enforce_rls`, and `adapter` was read by its own Test handler plus the manifest's own visibility predicates. Removing them changes no runtime behaviour, only the surface and the Test door's answers.
2. No path in this repository reads the stored row by key: no migration, export or reader names `enforce_rls`; the readers of `sys_platform_setting` (ownership tools, secret-reference union, upgrade-impact report, the read door) are key-agnostic and none acts on its value; `CLOUD_MANAGED_HIDDEN_SETTINGS` has no `knowledge` rule; the retrieval re-check has no switch to feed. RLS cannot be turned off by that row. Two limits, stated: the cloud overlay is not in this repository and was not measured, and a future manifest that re-declared a key named `enforce_rls` would resolve the stored `false` as a saved value; the exact-key-list test and the manifest header now stand against that. Security-touching: yes by the record rule (the hunks remove a control labelled as a security safeguard and state permission behaviour in docs and changeset); no vulnerability found.
3. Yes: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right, at the right level (patch with `!` and BREAKING, per the #37004 precedent), with the caller's new answer and a tidy-up note; N2 is the one gap.
4. Nothing keys on the manifest version: no reader of it in `service-settings/src`, and the Console (`SettingsView.tsx`) holds drafts in memory only, with no storage and no version check. All eleven locales drop the retired strings in step.
5. Right as the honest minimum, see N1 for the residue on PostgreSQL. The cloud sentence is card-worthy at low priority: nothing in `knowledge-turso` implements a per-organization fallback, the Test door's own answer says a blank URL opens `knowledge.db` and "never the platform database", so the manifest's English fallback contradicts the handler beside it. All eleven bundles already omit the sentence, so it reaches only raw-manifest readers and locales outside the eleven. File it: delete the sentence here, or have the cloud overlay supply it.
